# The mod API

Generated from `api/lce.api` by `tools/hooks/hookgen.py`; do not edit this file. API version 1.

How to use it from Lua and WebAssembly is in `modding.md`. A handle is a value that names a thing in the
game. A handle is valid only while the call or hook that gave it to you runs, except a `surface`, which lives until you destroy it or your mod is unloaded.
A result written `list:handle` is a list of those handles: a table in order in Lua, and a list value in WebAssembly (`lce.h`); an empty slot is nil.

## Handles

- `entity`: A living thing in the world, a player included.
- `level`: One dimension of the world.
- `chunk`: A 16 by 16 column of the world, while the game generates it.
- `primer`: The blocks of a chunk that a world generator is building, in chunk coordinates: 0 to 15 across and 0 up to its height.
- `surface`: A picture you own: a grid of pixels you write, which the game can draw anywhere it lets you draw. It lives until you destroy it or your mod is unloaded.
- `stream`: A channel to the speakers that you feed with sound. Sound you queue plays in order. It lives until you close it or your mod is unloaded.
- `canvas`: The world, while it is being drawn. Positions are world coordinates; the game places them relative to the camera.
- `painter`: The game's own menu kit, drawing in the interface pixels of the gui it came from: panels, buttons, sliders, boxes, scroll bars and text, in the style of the game's menus. It is valid until the next gui.painter call.
- `gui`: The heads-up display, while it is being drawn. Drawing in pixels of the interface scale.

### `ModRegistry.Open()`

content may be registered between Open and Close, which wrap the game's own item registration: a mod registers by hooking Item_staticCtor_after

### `ModRegistry.Close()`

The game's ModRegistry::Close.

### `registry.item(name: string, title: string, icon: string, stackSize: int)` -> bool

Add an item to the game, only from Item_staticCtor_after. Its id is your mod's id and name joined by a colon (mod:name; name is 1 to 32 of a-z 0-9 _), the same text /give takes. title is what players see, icon is the name of a game item whose picture it uses (stick, diamond, ...), stack is the most per stack, 1 to 64. The number the game gives it is chosen for each world and saved with that world, so it stays the same while mods come and go. False if the call came too late, the name is taken or a limit was reached.

### `registry.dimension(name: string, id: int)` -> bool

Declare a dimension, only from Item_staticCtor_after. id is its number (2 to 100, the game's own are -1, 0 and 1) and is what level:getDimension, entity:changeDimension and the packets carry; the dimension is named mod_name. It behaves like the overworld (terrain from generate_terrain, which a mod hooks and tells apart by the level it is given) and every Dimension_* hook can change that; its chunks are saved in the world under DIM<id>. At most 8 dimensions in all.

### `registry.item_of(name: string, kind: string, title: string, icon: string, a: float, b: float, c: float, d: float)` -> bool

Declare an item made from one of the game's own item classes, so it works the way that class does and a mod can change any of its methods with the Item_* hooks. kind food (a nutrition in half drumsticks, b saturation, c non-zero if it is meat), or sword, pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe (a mining level, b uses, c speed, d damage bonus: the item's own tier). icon is as in registry.item. kind can also be the name of an item already registered (mod:name, or just name for one of yours): the new item is made as that one is, with the same stack size.

### `registry.item_icon(name: string, image: surface)` -> bool

Give an item you registered a picture of its own, only from Item_staticCtor_after: the pixels of the surface (any size, scaled to the icon size) become the item's icon. Make the surface with surface.decode of a PNG. It also gives a picture to the item a block made with block_of places when that block's class has its own item (a door). The game adds rows to the end of its item picture sheet for these. False when the item is not yours or was not registered yet.

### `registry.block(name: string, title: string, texture: string, material: string, hardness: float, resistance: float, light: int)` -> bool

Add a plain full block, only from Item_staticCtor_after. Its id is mod:name, the text /setblock and /give take. title is its name, texture is the name of a game block whose picture it wears (stone, planks, ...), material is stone, wood, dirt, grass, sand, glass, metal, wool, ice, clay or snow (it sets how the block sounds and what it counts as), hardness is how long it takes to break (-1 never, 1.5 is stone), resistance to explosions, light 0 to 15 what it gives off. The block drops itself, and is saved in chunks by name.

### `registry.block_of(name: string, kind: string, title: string, material: string, hardness: float, resistance: float, light: int)` -> bool

Declare a block made from one of the game's own block classes, so it works the way that class does and a mod can change any of its methods with the Block_* hooks. kind is door, trapdoor, button, pressure_plate, lever, ladder or fence, or the name of a block already registered (mod:name, or just name for one of yours): the new block is made the same way and starts with that block's properties, pictures, shapes, drops and settings, which later calls change for the new block only. material, hardness, resistance and light are as in registry.block. The block looks like the game's own until a hook draws it differently.

### `registry.block_property(name: string, property: string, count: int)` -> bool

Give a block you registered a property with count values (0 to count-1), only from Item_staticCtor_after, before its textures. A block's properties multiply to at most 16 combinations. A property called facing (4 values: north, east, south, west; or 6 with up and down) is set from the way the player looks when the block is placed, so the block faces the player. Read and change it with level:get_state and level:set_state.

### `registry.block_drop(name: string, item: string, minimum: int, maximum: int)` -> bool

Choose what a block drops when it is broken, only from Item_staticCtor_after: min to max (0 to 64) of an item or block by name, a random number in that range. An empty name or max of 0 drops nothing. Without this a block drops itself.

### `registry.block_random_ticks(name: string)` -> bool

Give a block the game's slow random ticks, only from Item_staticCtor_after, so Block_tick is called for it now and then at random positions like grass growing. Everything else a block reports (a neighbour changed, placed, removed, an entity stepped on it or is inside it, a tick you asked for with level:schedule_tick) is a hook on the game class and needs no declaring: Block_neighborChanged, Block_onPlace, Block_onRemove, Block_stepOn, Block_entityInside, Block_tick, each given the block's name as self.

### `registry.block_power(name: string, property: string)` -> bool

Make a block a redstone power source whose strength (0 to 15) is the value of one of its properties, so set_state changes the signal. Needs a property of up to 16 values.

### `registry.block_interactive(name: string)` -> bool

Make a block take the click when a player right-clicks it with anything in hand, like a chest does, only from Item_staticCtor_after: block_use is called (and cancelling it is not needed), and nothing is placed against the block unless the player sneaks. Without this a block only sees block_use when an item is used on it, which is when the player holds something to place or use, and an empty hand does nothing.

### `registry.block_rotates(name: string)` -> bool

Make the shapes and the north, south, east, west and sides pictures of a block turn with its facing property (4 or more values; value 0 is the way you drew them, north), so you draw one shape and one set of pictures instead of one per facing. False when the block has no facing property.

### `registry.block_entity(name: string, slots: int)` -> bool

Give a block you registered a small store of its own for every block placed, only from Item_staticCtor_after: up to 64 keys of up to 32 characters, each holding text up to 1024 bytes, kept with the chunk and sent to the players who can see the block, so a client mod can read it with level:data_get too (every data_set sends an update; the game batches them per tick). slots is 0 for none, or 27 or 54 (the two sizes of the game's chest window) for an inventory the block holds, shown in the game's chest window with entity:open_container and read and written with level:get_item and level:set_item. Read and write it with level:data_get and level:data_set. Every placed block of this kind is ticked once a game tick on the server: hook ScriptedBlockEntity_tick and read its place with self:get_mPos_x(), get_mPos_y(), get_mPos_z() and its level with self:get_mLevel().

### `registry.block_shape(name: string, boxes: string, when: string)` -> bool

Give a block a shape that is not a full cube, only from Item_staticCtor_after, after its properties. boxes is up to 16 boxes joined by semicolons, each x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1 in sixteenths of a block (0 to 16, the low corner below the high), for instance "0,0,0,16,8,16" for a slab or "6,0,6,10,16,10;0,12,6,16,14,10" for a post with an arm. The boxes are what you collide with, what is drawn (each wears the block's side pictures) and what is outlined (their bounding box). when is empty or property=value for a shape used only in that state; a state beats none. A block with a shape does not hide the faces of its neighbours.

### `registry.block_face(name: string, side: string, texture: string, when: string)` -> bool

Choose the picture of one side of a block, only from Item_staticCtor_after: texture is the name of a game block whose picture to use. side is down, up, north, south, west, east, sides (the four around) or all; when is empty, or property=value to use it only in that state. The most specific match wins: a state beats none, a named side beats sides, and sides beat all. Properties must be added first.

### `ModBlocks.DeclareItemIcon(name: string, image: surface)` -> bool

the icon of the item a block of its own class places (a door), which a plain block item does not have

### `registry.block_texture(name: string, image: surface, side: string, when: string)` -> bool

The same as block_face with a picture of your own: the pixels of the surface (any size, scaled to the block texture size) are added as new rows at the end of the game's terrain picture sheet. For a block made with block_of, side is not a side but a slot: the picture the game's class reads, which the class defines once for every block of it (door: upper and lower, both needed; the other kinds have one picture, slot all). The block then draws as the class draws, with your pictures, and a block derived from it wears the same ones unless it supplies its own.

### `registry.block_model(name: string, model: string, picture: surface)` -> bool

Draw a block you gave a store (registry.block_entity) with a model of boxes of its own, only from Item_staticCtor_after, wearing a surface of yours: `texture <width> <height>` then a `part <name> <x> <y> <z> <u> <v> <dx> <dy> <dz> <width> <height> <depth> [head|legA|legB]` line for each box, as registry.entity_model takes it. The model is drawn at the block's centre, its pivots in sixteenths of a block with 24 as the ground, in addition to the block's own shape. False when the block is not yours, has no store or the text is not a model. A block derived from it has the same model.

### `registry.entity(name: string, base: string, health: float, speed: float)` -> bool

Add a kind of mob, only from Item_staticCtor_after: base is pig, cow, chicken, sheep, zombie, skeleton, spider or creeper, or a mob of a mod already declared (mod:name, or just name for one of yours), which the new one is made from the same class as, and any Entity_* hook answers a method of the game class, and the new mob is that mob (its model, sounds, drops and behaviour) under your own name mod:name, so /summon mod:name makes one, it is saved by name, and entity_spawn reports it with that name so you can clear its goals and give it new ones. health is its health in half hearts (1 to 1024) and speed multiplies the base mob's walking speed (0.1 to 10). At most 16 a mod set. Its network number is 200 plus its place in the sorted list of mod mobs, so a client must have the same mod mobs as the server.

### `registry.entity_texture(name: string, image: surface)` -> bool

Give a mob you declared with registry.entity a picture of its own, only from Item_staticCtor_after, laid out as the base mob's own texture is (a pig's picture for a pig-based mob, so nothing needs working out), at any size the base's layout scales to. A mob derived from it wears the same picture unless it gets its own. False when the mob is not yours or was not declared yet.

### `ModEntities.TextureOf(type: int, textures: Textures)` -> int

the texture a mod mob wears, or -1 for the one its renderer picks; call it while drawing

### `registry.entity_model(name: string, model: string)` -> bool

Give a mob you declared with registry.entity a model of boxes of its own, only from Item_staticCtor_after, in place of its base mob's, and give it a picture with registry.entity_texture. The text is a `texture <width> <height>` line then a `part` line for each box: `part <name> <x> <y> <z> <u> <v> <dx> <dy> <dz> <width> <height> <depth> [head|legA|legB]`. The part pivots at x y z (sixteenths of a block, y down, 24 is the ground), its box starts dx dy dz from the pivot and is width by height by depth, its picture starts at u v of the texture, and the last word moves it as the game's mobs move: the head turns with the mob's, legA and legB swing against each other. A mob derived from it has the same model. False when the mob is not yours or the text is not a model.

### `registry.entity_name(name: string, title: string)` -> bool

Name a mob you declared with registry.entity, only from Item_staticCtor_after, and give it a spawn egg: the egg is the game's own, in the creative menu and for /give, in the colours of the mob it is made from, and its name says "Spawn" and the title (a key translated by registry.translate, or the text itself).

### `registry.entity_spawn(name: string, category: string, weight: int, minimum: int, maximum: int)` -> bool

Let a mob you declared with registry.entity spawn by itself, only from Item_staticCtor_after, in every biome: category is monster (at night and in the dark), creature (on grass in daylight), water_creature or ambient; weight is its share of that category's chances (the game's pig has 10), and a group is minimum to maximum mobs (1 to 8). Chunks the world already made keep what they have.

### `registry.shaped(result: string, count: int, rows: string, key: string, group: string, like: string)` -> bool

Add a crafting table recipe, only from Item_staticCtor_after. rows is up to 3 rows of up to 3 symbols joined by / (a space is an empty slot), for instance "##/ S"; key says what each symbol is, as symbol=name joined by commas, for instance "#=minecraft:planks,S=mymod:ruby". result is a name too, count how many it makes. It joins the crafting menu's recipes like any other, in the tab group names (structures, tools, food, armour, mechanisms, vehicles or misc) and in the row of the item named like: the menu sorts a tab into rows by kind of item, and a mod item has no kind of its own, so name a game item of the kind you want it beside (for a lamp, minecraft:redstone_lamp; an empty like uses the result's own kind, which is a row of its own and is dropped when the tab has no row free). False when the call is too late or the text is malformed; a name no item or block has is reported in the log and the recipe skipped.

### `registry.shapeless(result: string, count: int, ingredients: string, group: string, like: string)` -> bool

Add a crafting recipe where the order does not matter, only from Item_staticCtor_after. ingredients is up to 9 names joined by commas; repeat a name to need more than one. group and like are as for shaped.

## Hooks

A hook is a point where the game asks mods before it decides. In Lua, `mod.hook("name", function(call) ... end)`; `call` has
the arguments by name, `call.cancel = true` stops what the game was about to do, and an argument marked `mut` can be assigned.

### `sound_start(sound: string, x: float, y: float, z: float, volume: float, pitch: float, kind: int)`

The game asks for a sound to be heard (kind 0 in the world, 1 on the interface, 2 music or a record). When a mod listens, the game's sound engine is replaced by the mod: nothing is played unless the mod plays it, with audio.open and sound.decode.

A provider: when a mod listens, the game uses the mod's work instead of its own.

### `generate_terrain(level: level, primer: primer, chunk_x: int, chunk_z: int)`

Make the terrain of a chunk. When a mod listens, the dimension uses this instead of the game's generator: the chunk starts empty and the mod fills it with primer:set_block. Structures, caves and decoration are the mod's to make; the game still lights the chunk and sets its biomes from the biome source.

A provider: when a mod listens, the game uses the mod's work instead of its own.

### `check_light(level: level, x: int, y: int, z: int, layer: int)`

The light at a position may have changed (a block was placed or removed, a chunk loaded; layer 15 sky, 0 block, the game's own numbers). When a mod listens, the world uses this instead of the game's light engine: read the surroundings with level:block_at and level:getBrightness, and store the result with level:set_light. Propagating to neighbours is the mod's to do.

A provider: when a mod listens, the game uses the mod's work instead of its own.

### `wire_update(level: level, x: int, y: int, z: int)`

A redstone wire was placed, removed or had a neighbour change. When a mod listens, the world uses this instead of the game's wire logic: work out the power of the wire network with level:wire_power, level:signal_at and level:conducts, write it with level:set_wire_power, then call level:update_wire_neighbors on what changed. A mod can do the whole network at once, which is how a faster redstone mod works.

A provider: when a mod listens, the game uses the mod's work instead of its own.

### `packet_encode(server: bool, loopback: bool, id: int, data: bytes (mut))`

A packet is about to be written to a connection. data holds its bytes in the game's own format; change them into whatever your protocol puts on the wire (compress, encrypt, rewrite, reframe) and the game sends your bytes with a length in front. Both ends must run the same mod, and packet_decode must undo it. server is true when the game is the server; loopback is true for the connection between the host and its own player in the same process, where a mod usually passes the bytes through; id is the game's packet number.

A provider: when a mod listens, the game uses the mod's work instead of its own.

### `packet_decode(server: bool, loopback: bool, data: bytes (mut))`

A packet's bytes arrived on a connection. data holds what the other side's packet_encode produced; turn it back into the game's own packet bytes (a packet number then its fields) and the game reads it as usual. loopback is true for the host's own player, and is the same on both ends of a connection.

A provider: when a mod listens, the game uses the mod's work instead of its own.

### `chunk_store(world: string, dimension: int, x: int, z: int, data: bytes)`

A chunk is to be saved. data is the chunk in the game's own serialised form (uncompressed); keep it wherever your format keeps chunks, for example with file.write. When a mod listens, the game does not write its region files at all. world names the world, dimension is 0 overworld, -1 nether, 1 end, and x and z are the chunk's position.

A provider: when a mod listens, the game uses the mod's work instead of its own.

### `chunk_fetch(world: string, dimension: int, x: int, z: int, data: bytes (mut), found: bool (mut))`

A chunk is to be loaded. Set data to the bytes chunk_store was given for it (or bytes in the game's format that you made) and found to true; leave found false and the game generates the chunk.
